title: ETRC: Goodyear FIA ETRC aces all set to light up Le Mans
summary: Sport news Part of the ever-popular 24 Heures Camions event, which also features races for the British and national championships, thousands of fans will watch the Goodyear FIA ETRC stars fight for on-track supremacy and vital points with  Norbert Kiss  in touching distance of becoming European champion for a record-extending eighth time.  But while Hungarian hero Kiss has his eyes on the overall title prize, the battle for Chrome category honours for drivers with less experience and fewer top overall results remains finely balanced. Ahead of the Le Mans weekend, defending champion  Mark Taylor  leads  John Newell  by a mere three points.  Having won 15 races and qualified on pole 10 times so far in 2026, Révész Racing-run Kiss has established an advantage of 105 points over fellow MAN-powered  Sascha Lenz  from Germany. With a maximum of 120 points up for grabs between Le Mans and the Jarama season finale from 2-4 October, Kiss can put this year’s Goodyear FIA ETRC title beyond the reach of his rivals with one round to spare.  Fourteen drivers will contest the four Goodyear FIA ETRC races at Le Mans. In addition to Kiss, Lenz, Newell and Taylor, they are former multiple champions  Antonio Albacete  and IVECO-powered  Jochen Hahn ,  Steffi Halm  and  René Reinert , who are among the race winners in 2026, top Young Driver  José Eduardo Rodrigues , double Zolder Chrome winner  Steffen Faas , his fellow German Chrome driver  Clemens Hecker  a, British duo  Luke Garrett  and  Bradley Smith , plus Mercedes-Benz-driving  Luis Recuenco  from Spain.  After banking two Goodyear FIA ETRC Chrome podiums at Circuit Zolder earlier this month, home hero  Jonathan André  will make the French championship his focus at Le Mans.  The TotalEnergies-supported driver highlighted the enormity of the 24 Heures Camions weekend. “It’s the main race of the season for me, a wonderful event. I will fight for the French championship, Jarama is next for me [in the Goodyear FIA ETRC]. As I am French, people are really pushing for me and there is always a very special atmosphere at Le Mans. It’s a great track to drive. It’s not the most complicated track, it’s difficult but Zolder is more difficult with all the kerbs and the slow chicanes. I like the tracks with no kerbs and Le Mans is a flat track for the motorbikes, like Misano, so I enjoy it, although the last corner is very tight, so the exit is very important. Just after Le Mans I will come to Jarama and the week after Jarama we have the final of the French championship in Albi. It’s busy and I try not to damage my truck.”     THE GOODYEAR FIA ETRC IN SHORT  Combining the excitement of truck racing with entertainment, sustainability and technical innovation, the Goodyear FIA ETRC is heavy metal motor sport at its very best, a truly unique spectacle and the pinnacle of global truck competition with 2026 marking the 20th full season since the current format was introduced.  With the Fédération Internationale de l’Automobile (FIA) assuming full control of the series, the Goodyear FIA ETRC enters an exciting new era in 2026.  As well as continuing to oversee the Goodyear FIA ETRC’s sporting and technical regulations, the global governing body for motor sport and the federation for mobility organisations worldwide is taking a more hands-on approach in running the championship.  Areas such as partnerships, calendar development, circuit relations, competitor engagement and paddock operations are all being managed directly by the FIA, part of efforts to strengthen the championship’s long-term growth by covering areas from sporting level to media exposure and sustainability.   SUSTAINABILITY AT THE HEART OF GOODYEAR FIA ETRC  Back in 2021, the Goodyear FIA ETRC became the first FIA-sanctioned motor sport series to switch to fully sustainable biofuel through a partnership with TotalEnergies, which continues in 2026.  All FIA ETRC drivers use Goodyear tyres incorporating 60 per cent sustainable materials, a five per cent increase compared to 2025, achieved through the use of carefully selected ingredients, such as silica produced from waste rice husk ash and carbon black sourced from alternative feedstocks. Goodyear retreads its racing tyres into standard truck tyres, thereby avoiding the practice of disposing of racing tyres.  Italian manufacturer IVECO, which introduced its electric S-eWay as the official Goodyear FIA ETRC pace truck in 2025, also remains a key partner.   KISS SHINES IN THE BELGIAN RAIN FOR EPIC GOODYEAR FIA ETRC VICTORY DOUBLE  Norbert Kiss took a giant step towards winning the 2026 Goodyear FIA European Truck Racing Championship with two heroic wet-weather drives at Circuit Zolder last Sunday (13 September). Having shared the race wins with Sascha Lenz the previous day, Kiss triumphed twice in the rain for a provisional lead of 105 points with two events and eight races remaining. After winning Race 3 from his 10th 2026 pole position, the Révész Racing-run Hungarian charged through from eighth to first in Race 4 for victory number 15 of the season, pulling off several spectacular overtakes in the process. Antonio Albacete and Lenz joined MAN-driving Kiss on the Race 3 podium after finishing second and third respectively with Lenz coming home second to the seven-time European champion in Race 4, one place ahead of IVECO-powered Jochen Hahn, who led for the first eight laps. Steffen Faas shone in the Chrome category with a victory double for tankpool24-Racing. By twice finishing second in the division, defending champion Mark Taylor completed the Belgian Truck Grand Prix weekend still leading the title standings, three points ahead of John Newell. After a rare error dropped him out of the Chrome podium fight in Race 3 – he finished fourth behind Jonathan André – Newell bounced back to place third in Race 4, securing the most fan votes to win the Goodyear Wingfoot Award ahead of Albacete and René Reinert. Kiss was followed home in Race 1 by Albacete and Hahn. Lenz, meanwhile, was restricted to seventh after a dramatic start to the opening contest when he ran through the gravel exiting the first corner in the battle for position. But he hit back in Race 2 to triumph ahead of Reinert, who resisted intense pressure from third-placed Hahn. After winning in the Chrome category for the first time this season at Autodrom Most last month, Newell finished first twice on Saturday. Championship rival Taylor was second in Race 1 ahead of André. Newell then topped an all-British podium in Race 2 with Taylor second and Luke Garrett third. Other notable performances in Race 1 came from José Eduardo Rodrigues, who finished fourth, and Reinert, whose capture of eighth place secured pole for the partially-reversed Race 2 grid. Kiss banked more important points with fourth place in Race 2.   FANS GET THEIR SAY WITH NEW-FOR-2026 GOODYEAR WINGFOOT AWARD   Already presented in several major series, including the FIA World Endurance Championship, European Le Mans Series and the British Touring Car Championship, the Goodyear Wingfoot Award is new to the Goodyear FIA European Truck Racing Championship for 2026 and recognises driver performance and achievement in the Goodyear FIA ETRC. At each of the seven Goodyear FIA ETRC events, a panel of experts from the FIA and Goodyear nominate three drivers following Race 3, based on their overall performance during the race weekend, their sporting behaviour and highlights on track. Fans will then be able to vote for their driver of the weekend via   Instagram   from the shortlist of candidates during Race 4. The winner is announced as part of the live broadcast coverage of Race 4 and presented with the Goodyear Wingfoot Award on the final podium. Norbert Kiss (Misano), Sascha Lenz (Slovakia Ring), Jochen Hahn (Nürburgring), Lukas Hahn (Most) and John Newell (Zolder) are the winners so far. GOODYEAR FIA ETRC DRIVERS LOOK AHEAD TO LE MANS Steffen Faas (Germany):  “I hope we have rain like in Zolder! Only a joke but we fix the truck and go to Le Mans directly from the IAA [in Hannover] and look what we can do there. I like the track, it’s nice, good safety and Zolder gives me good confidence.”   Jochen Hahn (Germany):  “Le Mans is one of my favourite circuits and we fight for second position in the championship. We were really too slow in the wet conditions at Zolder, so we must learn from these situations. But all is fine, all is good.”   Clemens Hecker (Germany):  “Le Mans is one of the biggest events in our season. With all the race fans there it’s so great. When you cross under the Dunlop bridge it’s very difficult to go in this next corner but it’s interesting and I like Le Mans. It’s great to be there.”   Norbert Kiss (Hungary):  “It’s the same like always, we try to do the best we can and if the title is coming then it’s coming. If we have some issues and we lose some points, then it’s okay. But I like Le Mans, it’s my favourite. I love it, the whole atmosphere and also the circuit itself is very nice and very smooth. I always love to race at Le Mans.”   Mark Taylor (Great Britain):  “We’ll go to Le Mans like we always do, take it track by track, the easiest way. We’ll have a look at the track, see what’s best for it, if we’re to go back with the set-up or stay as we are. It’s been a good track for me in the past but it’s like every race, you need a bit of luck as well.”     GOODYEAR FIA ETRC IN SHORT 4x7:  Seven rounds with four races per event (two races each day)  160 kph:  Safety-first approach means a speed limit of 160kph  1200bhp:  Power output of 1200bhp and torque of around 6000Nm  5300:  Minimum required racing truck total weight is 5300 kilograms, with a minimum of 3150 kilograms measured on the front axle  Qualifying format:  For Races 1 and 3 a three-stage qualifying format decides the grid: Q1/Q4: 15 minutes for all drivers; Q2/Q5: 10 minutes for the 12 fastest drivers from Q1/Q4; Q3/Q6: 5 minutes for fastest six drivers from Q2/Q5; grid positions for Races 2 and 4 decided by the results of Races 1 and 3 with the top-eight drivers lining up in reverse order  Titan or Chrome:  Drivers are either categorised as Titan or Chrome depending on their experience and level of success  Titles:  Four FIA titles for Overall and Chrome drivers, Young Driver and Teams  Goodyear Wingfoot Award:  Three drivers are nominated for the public vote on via   Instagram   during Race 4 based on their overall performance, sporting behaviour and highlights on track   GOODYEAR FIA ETRC ROUND SIX ESSENTIALS Venue:  Circuit Bugatti, Circuit des 24 Heures, CS21928, 720199 Le Mans Cedex 2, France  Website:   https://www.24h-camions.com/en   Date:  25-27 September 2026  Track length:  4.185 kilometres  Turns:  11 (6 right, 5 left)  Direction:  Clockwise  2025 winners:  Norbert Kiss x 2, René Reinert x 2  Tickets:  Click   HERE   for more information  In 100 words:  Rather than the 13.626-kilometre Circuit de La Sarthe, made famous by the 24 Hours of Le Mans sportscar race, France’s round of the Goodyear FIA ETRC – the penultimate event of the 2026 season – uses the 4.185-kilometre Circuit Bugatti. title: F1 - 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix Post - Qualifying Press Conference Transcript
summary: Sport news  DRIVERS    1 – George RUSSELL (Mercedes)    2 – Charles LECLERC (Ferrari)    3 – Oscar PIASTRI (McLaren)      PARC FERMÉ INTERVIEWS   (Conducted by Alex Brundle)      Q: George Russell, an absolutely thrilling lap. A gap of eight tenths of a second. Mr Saturday returns on Friday. That was a pretty special one, wasn’t it?    George RUSSELL:  Yeah, it’s been a while. It’s been a while, so it definitely feels good. It’s probably the biggest margin in my whole career, even including F2, F3 days. So, the lap felt really sweet. The car’s been feeling great this weekend and, on a track like this, when you can hook it up like that, it feels really amazing.      Q: You topped FP1, you topped FP2. A little bit more of a challenge in FP3, but it was never in doubt, was it?    GR:  I was feeling good. I was feeling good, to be honest. I think Max has been very fast this weekend. I don’t know what happened to him at the end, maybe, I think, with the yellow flag of Lando, he didn’t get that last chance, so it would have been interesting to see. But it was just the perfect lap at the end. I was in a good gap behind Hadjar, which gave me a nice little slipstream, probably by another tenth or two down this back straight. So, yeah, it was great.     Q: Charles, can we borrow you for a second? We saw a little bit of a tow for you across the line from Lewis Hamilton. Was that assistance up into the top three?     Charles LECLERC:  Honestly, it was quite a good lap. Lewis was in front, three, four seconds, I think, in front, and I managed to do a good lap at the end. But when I see the gap to George, maybe the lap wasn’t good enough. So, yes, but overall, we’ve been on the back foot all weekend. We kind of expected to be very far off after a difficult Friday, but this morning I had a little bit more hope. So, yes, I think in terms of position that’s where we expected to be but in terms of hap it’s a lot more than what we expected.       Q: How do you go about trying to race a Mercedes tomorrow that could be eight tenths up the road with a little bit more straight-line speed. is there a chance down into Turn 1 and get ahead, or are they going to be too far ahead on pace?    CL:  I mean, we’ll see. We’ll see tomorrow. Surely our straight-line speed is not our strength, but the pace has been quite strong in FP1 for the high fuel, so I hope it will be the case tomorrow.      Q: Oscar, you fooled us all again. You’ve been talking about how McLaren is struggling for pace all weekend, and here you are once again in the top three. That must have been a great lap.    Oscar PIASTRI:  Yeah, it was good. I think in qualifying we found a bit of pace. So, yeah, it’s not the first time that’s happened to us this year. We seem like we’re a bit on the back foot through practice, we come out in qualifying and, yeah, we just find that bit extra. And I was pretty surprised to see us one-two after the first lap of Q3, but unfortunately, we had no hope against George. So I’m very happy with how the weekend’s gone so far. It’s never easy around here, especially when it’s so gusty like today, so I’m very, very happy to be back in the top three.      Q: How much of a challenge was the wind out there? We saw a lot of moments for various drivers. Give us a feel for how difficult it is to drive these cars in the gusty conditions.    OP:  Yeah, I mean, honestly, trying to keep it between the lines, you know, the highway lines down the straights, is not easy. Especially, you know, it always sounds so dull talking about the wind in a Formula 1 car, but even when the walls disappear and you get a bit more open, you really get a massive gust. So, it’s not easy at all. You know, there’s 30 or 40 kph difference sometimes between laps, so you really got to be on your toes and adapt on the fly.      Q: George, I know you’ve only just finished qualifying, but pole position, a decent car underneath you, we’ve seen some pretty good race pace as well. Must be pretty confident going into tomorrow?    GR:  No, I’m feeling good. I think we’re in a great place to go for the win, but of course this is Baku and anything can happen. Of course, Charles is going to be motivated to probably throw one down the inside of Turn 1, but whatever happens, I feel confident that we can go for the win.      PRESS CONFERENCE        Q: George, what an extraordinary performance by you. Very well done. You said over the radio it was a very good lap. How did you do it?    GR:  Yeah, I mean, I’ve been feeling in a great spot this whole weekend. From FP1 I felt confident, I felt hooked up. You know, as I’ve said recently, I’m just getting more and more on top of this car and what it requires, and it’s just all feeling more intuitive. And, you know, I felt very confident we were in the running for pole, but when I crossed the line and I saw the gap, I was, yeah, I was shocked. I knew the lap was great. I had a nice slipstream at the end, which gave me an extra probably tenth and a half, two tenths, and it just all perfectly came together.      Q: Fine, you had a slipstream on that last lap that gave you a tenth, but you found a second from your first run in Q3 to that last lap. Where did that time come from?    GR:  It’s been a very challenging weekend with the tyres here for everybody. We only used one set of tyres in all of Q3. That was my third lap on the tyres. Most of these guys also did two laps on the tyres. I think it was only McLaren who pitted for a new set. But it was just like these tyres could keep on going and going, and we certainly were not sure what the right strategy was going to be come Q3, whether using two sets of tyres or keeping the same set on. But I just wanted to stick with what we knew. I knew my first lap wasn’t going to be the best because we had all of the fuel in the car, so I just kind of wanted to put a banker on the board because this track requires a lot of commitment. So, I just put a banker on the board and then, obviously, my next two laps were good enough for pole.      Q: Look, much pace. Does this feel like something of a breakthrough moment for you?    GR:  I wouldn’t necessarily say so. It’s definitely just being perfectly hooked up for me this weekend so far. But, you know, me and my team have put so much work in to help me get on top of the limitations, and I think since the summer break it’s been great. The performance has been substantially better than the results have shown. So, you know, it’s three front-row starts in the four races since the break. I’m very pleased with it.      Q: Looking forward to tomorrow, what sort of advantage do you expect to have over the field? Not as big as today.    GR:  No, for sure, for sure not as big as today. I think, looking back on yesterday’s practice, I think Verstappen was the biggest threat. I think he probably got a bit blocked, I think, by Lando with the yellow flag at the end, so didn’t have that chance to improve. But, yeah, I think we really don’t know. McLaren also threw out a big surprise at the beginning of Q3. They were one and two, and that was a surprise. But I feel Verstappen is going to be a threat. Obviously, you can’t discount Kimi. You know, started 19th in Monza and now he’s in 16th, so, yeah, he should be leading by a few laps early this time.      Q: George, very well done. Thank you very much for that. Charles, let’s come to you now. Your fourth front row this season. Just how was the car? How was that lap in Q3?    CL:  Well, I felt hooked up as well, but maybe not to the right hook when I see the gap with George. It’s quite a significant gap. So, yes, I mean, the car felt better than what it felt for the rest of the weekend. We’ve had our struggles this weekend and we were definitely not as competitive. But as George said, I think it’s very difficult to get these tyres in the right window, and particularly this weekend. I think probably McLaren and ourselves were a bit in the same boat, where we were really struggling in free practice. Some laps were good, but never really consistently there. And in qualifying I felt like we did a better job in that. But, yeah, it’s all relative, and eight tenths and a half is a lot. So, there are plenty of things that we should look at and try to improve, particularly because our weakness normally is straight-line speed, but today Sector 2 is also where George made the difference.      Q: Are there any areas of performance where your car has surprised you, either positively or negatively?     CL:  Overall, the predictability of the car this weekend it has been very difficult. Normally, I feel like one of my strengths coming here is being very precise and taking a lot of risk with the distance to the wall. This weekend I just couldn’t do that because the car was was not exactly reacting the way I wanted. It was just quite unpredictable. I still had that unpredictability in qualifying. It got better, but I couldn’t take the... yeah, I had to take a bit more margin compared to what I usually do here.      Q: Looking ahead to tomorrow’s race, how much confidence can you have? Do you have anything in your armoury that can help you challenge George Russell and Mercedes for the win?    CL:  We’ll try, and we’ll do our best. Whether that will be enough, only time will tell. But we know that we have a good race car, more often than not better in the race than in qualifying, and I hope that it will be the case again this weekend.      Q: Okay, Charles, thank you very much for that. And Oscar, let’s come to you now. Just one thousandth of a second from the front row for you. Very well done. Just how much of a surprise is this quali performance? Because the messaging from McLaren after practice wasn’t so positive.    OP:  Yes, it’s been not an easy weekend, for sure, from a few areas. You know, we’ve not been particularly quick. We’re also running cable ties on our car through Friday, which is never a great sign. So, it’s been a little bit of a tricky one for us. But it’s not the first time this year, I feel like, that we get to qualifying, we take all the fuel out and the car just comes alive more. You know, clearly compared to George and Mercedes, we’re still a long way off. But, yeah, it’s certainly not the first time where we get to qualifying and things look a bit brighter. So, yeah, happy with how we’ve tried to evolve this weekend. It’s certainly not been easy to get the most out of this car around here with how much you have to push and, obviously, the consequences. So, to end up P3 is a really good result.     Q: And in terms of your own confidence with the car, do you feel you’ve taken a step forward this weekend?    OP:  Yes and no. I mean, similar to what Charles said, to be honest, I think some laps here and there have been strong, but it’s been a lot in between that haven’t been very strong. And I feel like we’ve been reasonable at points, but, yeah, you know, our car needs some specific things, and trying to find those things on a street circuit is really tough. And again, I think in qualifying we just come alive a little bit more, everything becomes a little bit easier and it’s a bit easier for us to get the pace out of the car. But, no, on a personal level I feel like we’ve been building up well and, yeah, was pretty happy with my lap in Q3.      Q: And the different tyre strategy that you guys had compared to Mercedes, for example, how seriously did you consider just the one set of tyres in Q3?    OP:  We considered it. I mean, it was unclear for us as well what we wanted to do. I think Q2, we went back out on the used set of tyres and didn’t need a warm-up lap, and we were good to go and we improved. So I think we kind of just committed to... We managed to do a warm-up lap on the first set, which was good, but we knew we didn’t have time for that on the second set. But I think after that second run of Q2, we were relatively confident that we could at least nearly make it work. And we, you know, we didn’t really have any other option than to make it work. So I think for us that was a good idea.      Q: And where do you see your battles tomorrow? Can you challenge George?    OP:  If he’s got a tow bar that I can hook onto the back of, maybe. But, yeah, we’ll see what we can do. I think the Mercedes look incredibly quick here, but I think everyone else looks like they’re in a similar-ish kind of pack. And our race pace looked pretty good yesterday, to be honest. So, yeah, I think we can hang on and battle in the pack behind George and, yeah, see what lap Kimi starts coming through as well.      QUESTIONS FROM THE FLOOR       Q: (Sergey Podosenov – News.ru) My question to the three pilots. Baku is celebrating 10 years of Formula 1. What feels special to you about the atmosphere this anniversary weekend?     GR:  Well, I think Baku, as drivers, we do enjoy coming here because it’s a very unique circuit. It’s a unique Grand Prix. It’s different to a lot of others that we go to, and I think we also enjoy that. And the races are quite exciting as well, so it ticks quite a few boxes.   CL:  Yeah, same. I mean, not much to add. I think the track is really cool. It’s really challenging, and the castle part also makes it quite unique. So, yeah, it’s just a track I really enjoy driving.   OP:  Yeah, I mean, the other guys have said it. This year there seems to be a lot of Australians as well, which is cool. So, yeah, the Aussies are adding to the atmosphere as well.      Q: (Phil Duncan – PA) George, you said you needed a bit of luck to get back into this championship. Obviously, you’ve secured pole, you’ve got Kimi back in 16th. Do you feel as though the championship comeback starts now? And from Kimi’s side, do you think that’s a few signs of perhaps title jitters? I mean, I can’t recall many mistakes he’s made this season.    GR:  You know, I think the performance outside today was great, but, you know, he’s been flawless this whole season. I think when you look at every championship campaign, even for the winners, there are mistakes along the way. So, yeah, I still keep on believing and keep on fighting until it isn’t possible anymore. But I don’t feel any pressure. I feel excitement every time I jump in the car now, purely because I feel more confident in myself. And we spoke about it on Wednesday here: when that confidence starts to build, it’s just like this upward cycle. On the flip side, when you’re on the back foot, you start losing that confidence and then you start pushing the limits more, and that’s when mistakes happen. But, as I said, he’s been flawless this season. It’s the first mistake he’s made in a qualifying or race this whole year. So, yeah, let’s see tomorrow.      ENDS     FIA Formula One World Championship    Formula 1   SEASON 2026  Sport  Circuit 1SportFIA Formula One World ChampionshipCircuitSEASON 2026Formula 100 Friday, September 25, 2026 - 6:20pm  Friday, September 25, 2026 - 6:20pm

title: F1 – Russell dominates Baku qualifying as Antonelli crashes out in Q1
summary: Sport news George Russell claimed his fifth pole position of the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship with a commanding performance in Qualifying for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, beating Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc by 0.837s.  What initially looked like a four-team battle between Mercedes, Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull ultimately became a one-man show in Q3, as Russell found significant time on each of his final two runs. His 1:42.526s lap left Leclerc second, just 0.001s ahead of Oscar Piastri.  Isack Hadjar marked his return to competition with an impressive fourth place for Red Bull, ahead of McLaren’s Lando Norris. Lewis Hamilton qualified sixth for Ferrari, followed by Alpine’s Pierre Gasly, Max Verstappen, Williams’ Carlos Sainz and Franco Colapinto.  Russell’s dominant pole was made all the more significant by the early exit of Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli, who crashed at Turn 1 in Q1. The championship leader was unable to continue and will start the race from 16th.  Following a short delay, the opening 18-minute segment got under way on a warm and windy Baku track. Lance Stroll provided an early scare when he locked up and ran wide, although the Aston Martin avoided the barriers.  Hadjar set the initial benchmark with a 1:44.702s lap, while Alpine’s Gasly and Colapinto again showed the pace that had made them contenders for Q3 during practice.  Verstappen was unhappy with the behaviour of his Red Bull, reporting that the car was “bottoming like crazy” and that he was struggling to brake. Russell also complained of front locking before Antonelli brought out the first major interruption of the session.  The Italian lost control at Turn 1 and hit the wall, damaging the Mercedes. He attempted to return to the pits but was instructed to stop in a safe position, with race engineer Pete Bonnington confirming that the suspension could not be repaired in time.  Russell therefore carried Mercedes’ challenge alone. Verstappen, Hadjar and Hamilton all briefly moved ahead, but Russell responded on his final run to reclaim the top spot by mere thousandths.  At the other end of the order, Oliver Bearman escaped the elimination zone with a late improvement, leaving both Audi drivers out. Gabriel Bortoleto qualified 17th and Nico Hülkenberg 18th, while Alonso, Pérez, Bottas and Stroll were also eliminated.  With Antonelli’s Mercedes already out, the remaining 15 drivers returned for Q2. Russell again set the pace, establishing a 1:43.686s benchmark ahead of Leclerc, the two McLarens and Hamilton.  Hadjar continued his strong return, moving into third and just 0.194s off Russell to underline the closeness between the leading teams. Gasly also impressed for Alpine after benefiting from a tow from team mate Colapinto to move into seventh.  The battle for the final Q3 places was particularly close. Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad both fell short, with Lindblad unable to recover from another mistake. They were joined in elimination by Bearman, Williams’ Alex Albon and Haas driver Esteban Ocon.  Russell finished the segment fastest with a late 1:43.462s lap, two tenths ahead of Verstappen, setting up a potentially close fight for pole.  McLaren initially upset the order in the pole shoot-out, with Norris and Piastri moving ahead of Russell on their first attempts. Piastri’s 1:43.571s put him provisionally first, while Hadjar subsequently climbed to third.  Russell responded in emphatic fashion. His second run produced a 1:43.037s lap, around half a second faster than Piastri, before he found another five tenths on his final attempt to set the decisive 1:42.526s.  Leclerc improved to take second for Ferrari, while Piastri remained just 0.001s behind in third. Hadjar secured fourth, with Norris dropping to fifth after locking up on his final lap.  Hamilton was sixth ahead of Gasly and Verstappen, who could manage only eighth after encountering a yellow flag. Sainz put the upgraded Williams ninth, with Colapinto completing the top 10 for Alpine.  “It’s been a while, so it definitely feels good,” said Russell. “It’s probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even including F2, F3 days, so the lap felt really sweet. The car’s been feeling great this weekend, and on a track like this, when you can hook it up like that, it feels really amazing.”  Behind the top 10, Bearman qualified 11th ahead of Lawson, Albon, Ocon and Lindblad. Antonelli will start 16th after his Q1 crash, with Bortoleto and Hülkenberg behind.  The two Cadillacs will be promoted to 19th and 20th on the grid, with Sergio Pérez ahead of Valtteri Bottas, as Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll face grid penalties for power unit component changes.   2026 FIA Formula 1 Azerbaijan Grand Prix – Qualifying   1 George Russell Mercedes 1:42.526 - - 2 Charles Leclerc Ferrari 1:43.363 0.837  3 Oscar Piastri McLaren/Mercedes 1:43.364 0.838  4 Isack Hadjar Red Bull/Red Bull Ford 1:43.500 0.974  5 Lando Norris McLaren/Mercedes 1:43.672 1.146 6 Lewis Hamilton Ferrari 1:43.858 1.332 7 Pierre Gasly Alpine/Mercedes 1:44.047 1.521 8 Max Verstappen Red Bull/Red Bull Ford 1:44.081 1.555  9 Carlos Sainz Williams/Mercedes 1:44.566 2.040  10 Franco Colapinto Alpine/Mercedes 1:44.963  11 Oliver Bearman Haas/Ferrari 1:44.775  12 Liam Lawson Racing Bulls/Red Bull Ford 1:44.860 2.334  13 Alexander Albon Williams/Mercedes 1:45.001 2.475  14 Esteban Ocon Haas/Ferrari 1:45.016 2.490  15 Arvid Lindblad Racing Bulls/Red Bull Ford 1:45.106 2.580  16 Kimi Antonelli Mercedes - - - 17 Gabriel Bortoleto Audi 1:45.799 3.273  18 Nico Hülkenberg Audi 1:45.920 3.394  19 Sergio Pérez Cadillac/Ferrari 1:46.658 4.132  20 Valtteri Bottas Cadillac/Ferrari 1:48.290 5.764 21 Fernando Alonso Aston Martin/Honda 1:46.593 4.067 22 Lance Stroll Aston Martin/Honda 1:47.337 4.811       FIA Formula One World Championship    F1   SEASON 2026  Sport  Circuit 1SportFIA Formula One World ChampionshipCircuitSEASON 2026F101 Friday, September 25, 2026 - 5:49pm  Friday, September 25, 2026 - 5:49pm

title: F1 - Verstappen tops final practice for Azerbaijan Grand Prix ahead of Russell and Antonelli
summary: Sport news Max Verstappen set the fastest time in Free Practice 3 for the 2026 FIA Formula One Azerbaijan Grand Prix, denying George Russell a clean sweep of the practice sessions at the Baku City Circuit  The Red Bull driver posted a 1:43.922 in the closing stages of the hour-long session to finish 0.099s clear of Russell, with Lewis Hamilton a further 0.012s behind in third. Kimi Antonelli was fourth for Mercedes, ahead of Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc.  Following Russell’s double success on Thursday, Mercedes again showed strong pace during the early stages of the session, although the windy conditions around the Baku City Circuit continued to make life difficult for the drivers.  Running was initially limited, with Pierre Gasly setting the early benchmark for Alpine before the leading runners began to emerge. Leclerc moved to the top of the timesheets on the Soft tyres with a 1:45.564, while both Mercedes drivers initially ran the Medium compound.  Verstappen then briefly moved ahead as the drivers began to work on their qualifying preparations, with the long straight along the Baku waterfront providing opportunities for slipstreaming. Hamilton responded with a 1:45.093 to reclaim first place.  The changing conditions were evident throughout the session, with several drivers running wide at the circuit’s heavy braking zones. Verstappen reported that his Red Bull felt difficult to place through Turn 16, while Hamilton, Antonelli and Verstappen each explored the run-off areas at Turns 1, 4 and 15.  A brief Virtual Safety Car period was also required after a tree branch was blown onto the circuit, while Lance Stroll’s session came to an early end when the Aston Martin driver clipped the inside wall at Turn 1. Damage to his car prevented him from continuing, leaving him with just nine laps completed.  As the session approached its final 15 minutes, Mercedes switched both drivers to the Soft tyres for their qualifying simulations. Russell immediately moved to the top of the order with a 1:44.177 before improving again to 1:44.021.  Antonelli was unable to match his team-mate’s pace, while Verstappen moved between the two Mercedes cars with his first attempt on the Soft compound. The Red Bull driver then found further time on his final flying lap.  Verstappen set a 1:43.922 to move to the top of the timesheets, taking advantage of a slipstream on the long run towards the finish. Russell was unable to respond after running deep at Turn 7 on his final attempt, having also locked up into Turn 1.  Hamilton meanwhile improved to 1:44.033 to take third, just 0.012s behind Russell. Antonelli finished fourth on a 1:44.273, with Leclerc fifth on 1:44.544.  Pierre Gasly was sixth for Alpine, ahead of McLaren’s Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris. Isack Hadjar was ninth for Red Bull on his return to the RB22, with Alpine’s Franco Colapinto completing the top 10.  Carlos Sainz was 11th for Williams, followed by Oliver Bearman, Gabriel Bortoleto, Esteban Ocon, Nico Hülkenberg and Sergio Pérez.
